ui.footer: Possible issues, not a grade. No hint does not mean all code is correct.
ui.examplePrompt: Identify the parts in the example. Then apply the investigation question to your own code.
ui.none: No issues found within the supported checks.
ui.ideas: Explore these ideas. They are not errors.
ui.noIdeas: No principle suggestions here right now. You can enable them in settings.
ui.open: Open an HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python or C# file.
ui.failed: Analysis failed. Try CodeKompas: Nu analyseren in the Command Palette.
ui.large: This file exceeds the configured analysis limit.
ui.guide: Which patterns can CodeKompas help you check?
ui.guideIntro: Choose one pattern to check your code step by step.
ui.checkBefore: Inspect the highlight and the code just before it.
ui.recheck: Change one thing and check again.
ui.conceptReason: This concept appears in the highlighted code.
ui.conceptQuestion: What role does this play in your code? Explain your choice in your own words.

lessons.letters: Check the letters. Compare each letter with the declaration or fixed name in your course.
lessons.case: Check capitalisation. In case-sensitive names every letter must match the original spelling.
lessons.order: Check letter order. Read the name in chunks; two adjacent letters may have changed places.
lessons.missing: Is a letter missing? Compare the length and word parts with the original name.
lessons.extra: Is there an extra letter? Read the name slowly and compare each part.
lessons.repeated: Was a letter repeated accidentally? Double letters can be valid; compare with the declaration.
lessons.shape: Check the character shape. Decide whether it is a letter or digit and compare its shape and direction.
lessons.chunks: Check the order of the word parts. The same words in a different order form a different name.
lessons.separators: How are the parts joined? Check their boundaries and this language's convention, such as camelCase or snake_case.
lessons.reference: Did you rename this? Find the declaration and check that references use exactly the same name in the correct scope.
lessons.syntax: Check the structure. Also inspect the preceding statement: a missing symbol can cause a problem later.
lessons.quote: Where does this string or comment end? Find its opening and matching ending; later code may accidentally be inside it.
lessons.brackets: Do the brackets form pairs? Match opening and closing symbols of the same kind, working outwards.
lessons.htmlAttribute: How is the attribute value connected? Identify name and value separately and inspect the symbol between them; the name itself may be correct.
lessons.htmlTag: Is the tag fully delimited? A new line does not close a tag. Check where this tag ends and the next begins.
lessons.nesting: Check nesting. Follow the innermost element, then the order in which enclosing elements end.
lessons.duplicate: Is this repeated? An id should be unique; an attribute name should appear once in the same opening tag.
lessons.cssConnection: How are property and value connected? Split the declaration into these two parts and check the separator against CSS rules.
lessons.endStatement: Where does this statement end? Check whether two parts were accidentally joined and how the language separates them.
lessons.value: What value belongs here? Identify the expected value or expression and check whether it is complete.
lessons.color: Check the colour components. Inspect the number, order and separation of channels or the hexadecimal character count.
lessons.unit: Check number and unit separately. The unit determines how the measurement is interpreted; compare with your course.
lessons.cssCase: This is a convention, not invalid CSS. Standard properties usually use lowercase and hyphens. Custom CSS variables are case-sensitive.
lessons.indent: Check indentation. Show tabs and spaces and compare lines of the same block. In Python indentation also defines block structure.
lessons.block: Which statements belong to this block header? Check the transition to the block and the indentation of its first statement.
lessons.comparison: Do you intend assignment or comparison? State your condition in words and check the operator's meaning.
lessons.member: Are you continuing on the same object? Separating statements and accessing a property are different operations. Check the symbol between the parts.
lessons.callback: When should the function run? Check whether you pass the function or call it immediately and pass its result.
lessons.collection: One item or a collection? Check what the selection returns and which object receives the property access.
lessons.accessibility: What information does the image convey? Decide what someone without it needs to know and how to express that as alternative text.
lessons.convention: Check the convention. Valid code may be written differently; consider readability and project conventions.
lessons.logic: Does the operation match your intention? Describe input, operation and expected result separately.

concepts.naming: Naming: choose meaningful names and use them consistently. Existing API names are fixed.
concepts.callbacks: Callbacks: passing a function differs from running it immediately. Who decides when it runs?
concepts.collections: Collections: one item and a collection support different operations. Which level are you working on?
concepts.equality: Equality: distinguish assignment from comparison. In JavaScript the type may also affect comparison.
concepts.templates: Building text: distinguish fixed text and variable values. How does your language insert values into text?
concepts.destructuring: Destructuring: extract parts from an object or collection. Which data do you need?
concepts.selectors: Selectors: describe which elements you want. Consider zero results and multiple matches too.
concepts.boxmodel: Box model: content, padding, border and margin have different roles. Which space should change?
concepts.units: Units: decide whether a measurement is fixed or depends on text, container or viewport.
concepts.semantics: Semantics: HTML elements give content meaning. Choose based on the content's role.
concepts.accessibility: Accessibility: examine labels, alternative text and keyboard use. Does the page work without a mouse or vision?
concepts.styling: Separating styles: shared classes can replace repeated direct styling. Which choices should change together?
concepts.functions: Functions: group a clear task. Parameters receive input; returning a result differs from printing text.
concepts.arrays: Arrays: store values in an ordered collection. Check indices, length and an empty collection.
concepts.objects: Objects and classes: group related data and behaviour. What responsibility does this object have?
concepts.conditions: Conditions: decide when code runs. Test true and false conditions and boundary cases.
concepts.loops: Loops: repeat a task with progress and a stopping condition. What happens in the first and last iteration?
concepts.dom: DOM: the browser represents the page as an object tree. Selecting, changing and creating are distinct steps.
concepts.json: JSON: text-based data exchange differs from an object in memory. In which direction are you converting?
concepts.async: Async: an operation may wait for an external result. Where do you need the result and what if it fails?
concepts.scope: Scope: a name is not available everywhere. Check where it is declared and used.
concepts.layout: Layout: distribute space and relate parts. Also test a narrower viewport and longer content.
concepts.cascade: Cascade: several CSS rules can affect one element. Examine inheritance, specificity and rule order.
concepts.es6: ES6: choose variable declarations based on scope and mutability. Older syntax is not automatically wrong.
concepts.dry: DRY: check whether repeated code serves the same purpose. A shared approach can then simplify changes.
concepts.tokens: Design tokens: give recurring colours and sizes shared meaning. CSS variables help manage these choices together.
concepts.bem: BEM: class names distinguish block, element and modifier. It is a naming convention, not mandatory architecture.
concepts.components: Components: a reusable part has a clear task and boundary. What data does it receive?
concepts.gestalt: Gestalt: proximity and similarity support grouping. View the page in the browser; CodeKompas cannot see the rendered design.
concepts.events: Events: an event triggers a response. Which action do you observe and what task does the handler perform?
concepts.types: C# types: a type determines values and operations. With var the compiler infers the type; the variable is not untyped.
concepts.exceptions: Exceptions: an error interrupts normal execution. Handle expected errors specifically and choose a useful next step.
concepts.imports: Imports: names may come from other files or libraries. Check their source and alias; CodeKompas does not resolve the whole project.
concepts.pyBlocks: Python blocks: indentation groups statements. A continuation inside brackets is not a new block.
concepts.pyNames: Python names: functions and variables often use snake_case; classes use PascalCase. Uses must match the definition exactly.
concepts.csNames: C# names: local variables often use camelCase; types and methods use PascalCase. Existing .NET names are case-sensitive.
